classification.difficultyReason: Infer the centre and radius of each interval and encode open or closed endpoints in an absolute-value inequality.

content.prompt: Describe the following subsets of the number line in the form $|x-a|<r$ or $|x-a|\le r$.

spec.description: Horizontal number line with labelled ticks from -4 to 4 and an open-ended segment from -2 to 2 above the axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied interval is a permanent question given; its absolute-value description is hidden in the answer.

answer.worked:
The open endpoints exclude both boundary values. The centre and radius are
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{-2+2}{2}=0\\r&=\frac{2-(-2)}{2}=2.\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $|x|<2$.

spec.description: Horizontal number line with labelled ticks from -4 to 4 and a closed segment from -2 to 0 above the axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The closed interval is a permanent question given; the response inequality is hidden.

answer.worked:
The filled endpoints include both boundary values. The centre and radius are
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{-2+0}{2}=-1\\r&=\frac{0-(-2)}{2}=1.\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $|x+1|\le 1$.

spec.description: Horizontal number line with labelled ticks from -4 to 4 and an open-ended segment from -4 to 2 above the axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied interval is visible; its absolute-value description is hidden.

answer.worked:
The open endpoints give a strict inequality. The centre and radius are
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{-4+2}{2}=-1\\r&=\frac{2-(-4)}{2}=3.\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $|x+1|<3$.

spec.description: Horizontal number line with labelled ticks from -4 to 4 and a closed segment from 1 to 4 above the axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied closed interval is visible; its absolute-value description is hidden.

answer.worked:
The filled endpoints give an inclusive inequality. The centre and radius are
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{1+4}{2}=\frac52\\r&=\frac{4-1}{2}=\frac32.\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $\left|x-\frac52\right|\le\frac32$.

spec.description: Horizontal number line with labelled ticks from -4 to 4 and an open-ended segment from -3 to 2 above the axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied interval is visible; its absolute-value description is hidden.

answer.worked:
The open endpoints give a strict inequality. The centre and radius are
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{-3+2}{2}=-\frac12\\r&=\frac{2-(-3)}{2}=\frac52.\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $\left|x+\frac12\right|<\frac52$.
